definitions.plain_definition: When things are connected, ordered, and working together in a meaningful way.
definitions.used_in_context: If coherence is good — measurably, physically, across every domain — then how did Western culture arrive at a place where tearing down structure is called liberation?

definitions.plain_definition: The process where order and connection break down into randomness and disorder.
definitions.used_in_context: How an entire civilization convinced itself that decoherence is freedom, entropy is liberation, and the destruction of structure is progress.

definitions.plain_definition: A measure of disorder or randomness in a system; things naturally tend to become more disordered over time.
A physics rule that says disorder (entropy) always increases in a closed system unless energy is added from outside.
definitions.used_in_context: Without external input, systems move toward maximum entropy. The Great Inversion isn't a moral failing — it's the default behavior of any system that disconnects from its coherence source.

definitions.plain_definition: The opposite of entropy; the process of creating order and reducing randomness, which requires energy from outside the system.
definitions.used_in_context: The only thing that reverses entropy is external energy input. The only thing that reverses moral decoherence is external coherence input. Physics calls it negentropy. Theology calls it grace.

definitions.plain_definition: When information is consistent, true, and fits together logically.
When relationships are stable, faithful, and have clear boundaries that keep them healthy.
When a society has shared values, norms, and structures that keep it stable and functioning.
When there are shared standards of beauty that are not just personal opinion.
When religious beliefs are consistent, logical, and based on a sacred order.
A chain reaction where denying one objective truth leads to denying all objective truths in every area of life.
definitions.used_in_context: Once you deny that truth is objective (informational decoherence), everything downstream collapses. If truth is subjective, then morality is subjective. If morality is subjective, then beauty is subjective. If beauty is subjective, then meaning is subjective.

definitions.plain_definition: A theoretical end state of the universe where everything is evenly spread out, no energy differences exist, and no life or structure is possible.
definitions.used_in_context: Physics has a word for maximum relativism: heat death. Every particle at the same temperature. No gradients. No structure. No information. No life.

definitions.plain_definition: A medical condition where the body's immune system mistakenly attacks its own healthy cells.
definitions.used_in_context: In biology, this is called an autoimmune disorder — when the body's defense mechanisms are tricked into attacking the body itself.

definitions.plain_definition: A metaphor for a society that attacks its own healthy structures and values, thinking it is making progress.
definitions.used_in_context: The Great Inversion is a civilizational autoimmune disorder.

definitions.plain_definition: The breakdown of shared moral standards, leading to confusion about right and wrong.
definitions.used_in_context: The only thing that reverses moral decoherence is external coherence input.

definitions.plain_definition: The breakdown of healthy relationships, leading to isolation and loss of love.
A widespread feeling that life has no purpose or significance.
definitions.used_in_context: Rising rates of anxiety, depression, suicide, addiction, loneliness, institutional distrust, family dissolution, meaning-crisis.

definitions.plain_definition: In Christian theology, the free and unearned help and love from God that can restore order and goodness.
definitions.used_in_context: The only thing that reverses moral decoherence is external coherence input. Physics calls it negentropy. Theology calls it grace.
